title: Per-tenant burst matrix and queue isolation follow-up to prevent cross-tenant surge amplification
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: During a regional capacity event on 2026-02-27 we observed a cross-tenant surge amplification where aggressive burst requests from a small set of tenants caused tenant-agnostic quota windows to exhaust and cascade into 429 storms for unrelated tenants. Root cause analysis shows two contributing issues: (1) a global sliding window counter used for short-term bursts that attributed tokens aggregated across tenants in the same bucket, and (2) a shared in-memory request queue with FIFO fairness that allowed noisy tenants to monopolize processing during transient spikes. This ticket defines the follow-up work: per-tenant burst matrix, queue isolation per tenant priority class, and a soft-landing circuit policy to avoid synchronized resets that amplify retries.
action_items: Design and implement a per-tenant burst matrix: map tenant -> (short_window_capacity, short_window_burst_limit, replenishment_rate) (owner: Diego Morales, estimate: 3)
Introduce tenant-isolated request sub-queues within each gateway worker and enforce per-queue admission control to prevent head-of-line blocking (owner: Priya Singh, estimate: 2)

Add a soft-landing circuit policy: on short-window exhaustion, transition tenant to degraded-but-functional mode with rate-limited background retries, avoiding global resets (owner: Liam O'Connor, estimate: 1)
Extend telemetry: expose per-tenant short-window utilization, queue-depth histograms, and a per-tenant retry amplification metric for 95th and 99th percentiles (owner: Maya Chen, estimate: 1)
Create synthetic load tests that simulate 1% noisy tenants producing 10x bursts to validate isolation and no cross-tenant error amplification (owner: Diego Morales, estimate: 1)
Update runbooks and automated incident alerts: add a runbook step to identify burst-matrix exhaustion and an automated mitigation to promote canary to global if safe (owner: Asha Patel, estimate: 1)
Post-deploy bake and verification: 72h observation window with specified dashboards and success criteria before full rollout (owner: Diego Morales, estimate: 0)

2026-03-10 Asha Patel: Added canary alert thresholds to Grafana dashboard: dashboard/gw-burst-matrix. If per-tenant retry amplification > 20% for 10m during canary, we will auto-rollback and alert SRE.

2026-03-10 Security review comment (Olivia Park): Memory isolation looks reasonable but we need to add quota enforcement for large tenant metadata to avoid OOM when creating queues. Added a dependency on ENG-613500.

2026-03-10 Diego Morales: Noted remaining work: contract tests for the graceful downgrade API, docs for on-prem customers about enabling burst-matrix, and an RFC for tenant SLA exemptions. Planning follow-up tickets.
2026-03-10 Asha Patel: Moving status to In Progress. Will coordinate rollout schedule and Slack incident channel for live monitoring during canary.

acceptance_criteria: No increase in customer-visible 429s for top-200 tenants during 72h canary compared to baseline
Per-tenant short-window utilization metric present and emitting at 1s granularity
Synthetic noisy tenant test shows <2x amplification of errors compared to baseline and no cross-tenant 429 spikes
Runbook updated with steps to identify burst-matrix exhaustion and automated mitigation hooks
